facts.fact_text: Opposition demonstrations were held in Azerbaijan on 2 April 2011.
Despite their peaceful character, demonstrations held without authorisation were dispersed by the police.
According to the applicants, they had intended to attend the demonstration scheduled for 2 April 2011.
According to the applicants, the first applicant was involved in the organisation of the demonstration scheduled for 2 April 2011.
Prior notice of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 had been given to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.
The first applicant alleged that between approximately 10 a.m. and 11 a.m. on 31 March 2011, after he had taken his child to kindergarten, police officers stopped his car.
At around 2 p.m. on 31 March 2011, the first applicant learned that he would not be released from detention.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
The second applicant alleged that at around 10.30 a.m. on 31 March 2011, when he was still in bed, three police officers entered his apartment without an arrest warrant.
The police officers took the second applicant to police station no. 3 of the Sumgait City Police Office on 31 March 2011.
The Sumgait City Court sentenced the second applicant to seven days' administrative detention.

The third applicant alleged that when he had been outside the Sumgait City Police Office and no longer accompanied by his lawyer, police officers arrested him without explaining the reasons for doing so.
The third applicant alleged that police officers took him to police station no. 4 of the Sumgait City Police Office after arresting him on 31 March 2011.
The Sumgait City Court sentenced the third applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
According to the official records, the first applicant was arrested for disobeying a lawful order of a police officer.

The administrative-offence report issued by police officer T.A. stated that the first applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.

At the material time, Article 396.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an authorised official may use administrative arrest as a measure to prevent administrative offences, to establish the identity of a person, to draw up an administrative-offence report if this cannot be done at the place of the administrative offence and if the drawing up of a report is important, to ensure the correct and timely examination of administrative-offence cases, and to ensure the implementation of decisions in administrative-offence cases.

At the material time, Article 398.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that administrative arrest, that is the short-term restriction of an individual's liberty, may be applied in exceptional circumstances when deemed necessary for ensuring the correct and timely examination of an administrative-offence case or for the implementation of a decision in an administrative-offence case, except for instances set out in legislation.

At an unspecified time on 31 March 2011, the first applicant was informed that he was being detained in connection with the upcoming demonstration of 2 April 2011.
During questioning on 31 March 2011, the first applicant was asked about his intention to participate in the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
In his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant argued that he had been arrested in connection with the demonstration scheduled for 2 April 2011.
The second applicant stated before the Sumgait City Court that at the police station he had been questioned about his political activity.
The third applicant stated before the Sumgait City Court that he believed the motive for his arrest had been his participation in the demonstration of 12 March 2011.

According to the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe's document CommDH(2011)33 of 29 September 2011, the Commissioner's attention was drawn to the wave of arrests of activists and political opponents in connection with protests held in Baku in March and April 2011.

The European Parliament Resolution of 12 May 2011 on Azerbaijan (P7_TA(2011)0243) noted that a wide-ranging clampdown on freedom of expression and assembly was being carried out in Azerbaijan following the peaceful protests against the government on 11 March and 2 April 2011.
The European Parliament Resolution of 12 May 2011 on Azerbaijan deplored the arrest of around 200 people prior to, and during, the anti-government protests of 2 April 2011 in Baku.

According to the Amnesty International public statement EUR55/003/2011 of 31 March 2011, ahead of the 2 April protest organised by opposition political parties through Facebook, the Azerbaijani authorities detained at least 11 prominent political activists on 31 March 2011.

According to the Human Rights Watch news release of 1 April 2011, Azerbaijani authorities detained at least 10 opposition activists in an effort to prevent a public rally planned for 2 April 2011 in Baku.

According to the Human Rights Watch news release of 1 April 2011, the activists were quickly convicted in summary trials on charges of disobeying police orders and sentenced to administrative detention ranging from five to thirteen days, which would keep them locked up beyond the protest date.

According to the Amnesty International press release of 2 April 2011, John Dalhuisen stated that the fact that key organisers were being arrested in advance and sentenced in closed trials of offences that had yet to take place was indicative of the length to which the authorities were prepared to go to silence dissenting voices.

According to the Human Rights Watch news release of 12 March 2011, in at least three cases the Azerbaijani authorities held activists on administrative charges just long enough to prevent them from participating in the planned protests.

According to the Contact online news release of 31 March 2011, the chief of the press service department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, Orkhan Mansurzade, informed the Turan news agency that attempts to breach public order and to hold a protest on 2 April 2011 at the central streets and squares of Baku without agreement of the Baku City Executive Authority would be vigorously prevented.

According to the Contact online news release of 31 March 2011, the mayor's office refused to give permission to the Ictimai Palata to hold a demonstration on 2 April 2011 in front of Narimanov cinema and proposed to hold the protest in Bibiheybet settlement.
According to the Contact online news release of 31 March 2011, the Ictimai Palata decided to hold the protest at 2 p.m. on 2 April 2011 at the Fountains Square.

According to the Contact online news release of 31 March 2011, in connection with the Ictimai Palata's decision to hold the protest at the Fountains Square on 2 April 2011, arrests of potential activists began.
